statement: Subtree-aware split, decided before any policy file exists (PLAN.md §9). Whole branches are held out: holding out a child whose parent is in dev means replay can never reach it and the holdout measures nothing.
rule: Hold out whole branches, never random nodes.

recorded_only.op1b-seventh-defect-repair: Appended after this split was frozen. It is a repair node on the dev spine, so adding it to dev would not touch the holdout - but it would be a post-hoc edit of a pre-registration record, and its quality term is 0, so it would change no policy's V. Recorded, not smuggled in. Guard 14 enforces that every node is in exactly one of dev / holdout / recorded_only, so this exclusion stays visible and intentional.

amendments.rule: A node discovered after the split joins dev if its parent is in dev. The holdout never grows: a class the policy has not seen stays unseen, which is the only property this file exists to protect.
amendments.why: Dream-RSI's premise is that the pool expands as discovery proceeds (§1), so a frozen dev side is not the intent - a frozen holdout is. op2d is the first node in the tree with a positive quality term (s_v = 0.17), so excluding it would have left the loop's only live channel outside the pool.

amendments.rule: Same rule as the first amendment: a node discovered after the split joins dev if its parent is in dev; the holdout never grows.
amendments.why: op2e is the ceiling for op2d, so it belongs in the branch the policy may learn on. Its quality term is 0 (it is a negative result), so it only adds the cost of reaching it.

amendments.rule: Same rule: parent in dev -> dev; the holdout never grows.
amendments.why: A correction node is part of the discovery history the pool records.

amendments.rule: Same rule: parent in dev -> dev; the holdout never grows.
amendments.why: The exhaustive version of op2b belongs in the branch it completes.

why.dev: The spine. Everything downstream of op1 exists because op1 was flat, so it cannot be learned from any other branch.
why.op3-frame-sharing: Kober's recorded relation on a deciphered script. The real generalisation test: can a dev-tuned policy triage a class it has never seen? (op3a rides with it — same branch.)
why.op4-slot-alternation-A: Ventris's actual method, and the most surprising negative. It must not be visible while the policy is tuned.
why.op4b-minimal-pair-B: Exists because A failed its own permutation control. Holding out the parent and not the child would make the child unreachable.
why.x1-cm-corpus: Tests whether the policy ever chooses to stop searching and go get data. If a dev-tuned policy never selects it while every class is flat, the loop has learned to thrash (PLAN §9.3).
why.x2-anetaki-ii: Second acquisition option, so 'get data' is a choice and not a single named action.
why.x3-bilingual-find: Third, child of x1: semantic anchors are evidence class #1 in the closure paper §7.
